headline: Town committees reviewed rising costs for major park, golf, and trail projects, while housing and wastewater proposals were deferred past fall Town Meeting.
synopsis: The Community Preservation Committee reviewed updated funding requests for three major projects heading toward fall Special Town Meeting, as projected costs climbed for Fay Memorial Park, Southborough Golf Course irrigation, and the Peninsula Trail footbridge. The Affordable Housing Trust decided to shift proposed revisions to the 55-plus housing bylaw to spring Town Meeting, while the Wastewater Study Committee also confirmed it will not bring any funding requests to the fall warrant. Meanwhile, the Community Preservation Committee resolved a wording dispute by voting 5-1 to credit Southborough residents on upcoming library plaques, matching the Library Board of Trustees preference. The Library Trustees also backed a future two-hour closure for staff dementia training and approved two internal promotions.

highlights.title: Fay Memorial Park project estimate rises to $1.5 million
highlights.why: Revised plans added $240,000 for parking reconfiguration and road alterations along Central Street, bringing the overall estimate to about $1.5 million ahead of fall Special Town Meeting.

highlights.title: Golf course irrigation estimate climbs to $976,470
highlights.why: After previous bids exceeded the $553,000 approved in 2024, revised estimates increased sharply due to new pump station needs, prompting a request for additional Community Preservation Act funding.

highlights.title: Peninsula Trail footbridge scope revised amid higher costs
highlights.why: The Trails Committee eliminated a planned boardwalk to lower costs, presenting a revised $434,328 footbridge budget that requests $178,496 in supplemental Community Preservation Act funds.

highlights.title: Wastewater committee defers fall Town Meeting proposal
highlights.why: The committee confirmed it will not bring funding requests or financing districts to fall Special Town Meeting, choosing instead to consult MassDEP on watershed discharge restrictions along Route 9.

highlights.title: Proposed 55-plus housing bylaw revisions shifted to spring
highlights.why: The Affordable Housing Trust decided to target the spring 2027 Annual Town Meeting to work with the Planning Board and town counsel on removing unit caps and refining affordability rules.

highlights.title: Committee approves library plaques crediting Southborough residents
highlights.why: The Community Preservation Committee voted 5-1 to endorse bronze plaque wording thanking Southborough residents rather than taxpayers for prior facade and history collection funding, agreeing with library trustees.
